description:
The Mangalya Scheme for Widow Remarriage is a significant welfare initiative launched by the Government of Madhya Pradesh in India. 

The scheme was officially launched on 25th October 2008. 

It aims to provide support and encouragement for the remarriage of widows. 

The initiative is rooted in the social context of improving the status of widows in society. 

Historically, widows in India have faced social stigma and economic challenges. 

The Mangalya Scheme seeks to address these issues by promoting remarriage and providing financial assistance. 

The primary objective of the Mangalya Scheme is to facilitate the remarriage of widows. 

The government aims to empower widows and help them reintegrate into society. 

The scheme specifically targets widows aged between 18 and 55 years. 

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to increase the number of remarriages among widows. 

The government has set a goal to assist at least 10,000 widows annually under this scheme. 

The financial assistance provided under the Mangalya Scheme is substantial. 

Eligible widows receive a one-time financial grant of INR 50,000. 

This amount is intended to support the expenses associated with remarriage. 

In addition to the financial grant, the scheme also provides social support. 

The government organizes awareness programs to change societal perceptions about widow remarriage. 

The eligibility criteria for the Mangalya Scheme are clearly defined. 

Applicants must be widows residing in Madhya Pradesh. 

They must be between the ages of 18 and 55 years. 

The income limit for eligibility is set at INR 2 lakh per annum. 

Widows must not have remarried previously to qualify for the scheme. 

The application process for the Mangalya Scheme is straightforward. 

Interested applicants must fill out a prescribed application form. 

The application form can be obtained from the local Social Welfare Department offices. 

Applicants are required to submit several documents along with the application. 

These documents include a copy of the widow's death certificate of the deceased husband. 

A copy of the applicant's identity proof is also necessary. 

Income proof must be submitted to verify eligibility. 

Additionally, applicants must provide a recent passport-sized photograph. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the local authorities. 

The processing time for applications typically takes about 30 days. 

Disbursement of the financial assistance occurs shortly after approval. 

The funds are transferred directly to the bank account of the eligible widow. 

The Mangalya Scheme is implemented by the Department of Women and Child Development. 

This department is responsible for overseeing the welfare of women in Madhya Pradesh. 

Contact details for the department can be found on the official government website. 

The scheme has seen a positive response since its inception. 

Many widows have benefited from the financial assistance provided. 

The government has reported an increase in the number of remarriages among widows. 

Awareness campaigns have played a crucial role in changing societal attitudes. 

The Mangalya Scheme is part of a broader initiative to empower women in India. 

It aligns with the government's commitment to gender equality and women's rights. 

The scheme also complements other welfare programs aimed at women. 

For instance, it works alongside schemes like the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao initiative. 

The Mangalya Scheme has been recognized for its innovative approach. 

It not only provides financial support but also addresses social stigma. 

The government continues to monitor the effectiveness of the scheme. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the program. 

The Mangalya Scheme represents a significant step towards social reform. 

It encourages the idea that widows can lead fulfilling lives post-marriage. 

The scheme has also inspired similar initiatives in other states. 

Overall, the Mangalya Scheme for Widow Remarriage is a comprehensive welfare initiative. 

It provides financial assistance and promotes social change. 

The scheme has the potential to transform the lives of many widows in Madhya Pradesh. 

By facilitating remarriage, it aims to restore dignity and hope. 

The Mangalya Scheme is an important example of targeted welfare policy. 

It reflects the government's commitment to improving the lives of marginalized groups. 

The scheme is a vital component of the state's social welfare framework. 

It highlights the importance of addressing both economic and social challenges. 

The Mangalya Scheme stands as a beacon of hope for many widows. 

It empowers them to take control of their lives and futures. 

The financial assistance provided can significantly alleviate their economic burdens. 

The scheme fosters a supportive environment for remarriage. 

It encourages society to embrace change and support widows. 

The Mangalya Scheme is a testament to the power of government intervention. 

It demonstrates how targeted initiatives can lead to meaningful change. 

The scheme continues to evolve based on the needs of its beneficiaries. 

It remains a crucial tool in the fight for women's empowerment in India. 

The Mangalya Scheme for Widow Remarriage is a model for similar programs nationwide. 

It exemplifies the importance of addressing social issues through comprehensive policy. 

The scheme is a vital resource for widows seeking a new beginning. 

It empowers them to rebuild their lives with dignity and support. 

The Mangalya Scheme is a significant contribution to social justice in India. 

It represents hope for a better future for widows across the state.
